A Concur renewal notice is usually when the question gets real. You're leaving an incumbent that has likely run your expenses for years. SAP has owned it since[SAP completed its acquisition of Concur](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1066026/000119312514433565/d833534dex991.htm) on Dec. 4, 2014.


The hard part about comparing SAP Concur alternatives is that most lists rank tools as if every buyer left for the same reason. A team frustrated by per-report costs needs a different replacement than one whose travelers won't book in Concur Travel.


So the options below are grouped by replacement type, covering travel-and-expense suites, card-led platforms, and expense-only tools. For a broader view, see[our ranking of seven expense management platforms](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/best-expense-management-software) . A decision matrix and a migration checklist follow the groups.


**Key Takeaways**


-


Navan (navan.com), the corporate travel and expense company formerly called TripActions, Perk (formerly TravelPerk), and Emburse replace Concur Travel and Expense together.


-


Ramp, Brex, and Corpay bundle a card program with expense, so decide early whether your current cards stay.


-


Expensify, Zoho Expense, Sage Expense Management (formerly Fyle), and Rydoo replace the expense tool and keep your cards.


-


Per-report and per-user pricing scale differently, so model both against your own volume.


-


Booking can stay on Concur Travel or move, and that call comes before vendor demos.


-


Plan the cutover around open reports, card feeds, approval chains, and ERP mapping.


## Why do companies look for SAP Concur alternatives?


Finance teams usually leave Concur for one of four reasons. They want clearer cost scaling, less configuration overhead, a card program and expense tool under one roof, or booking and expense in one app.


Concur publishes per-report starting prices for its Base and Plus editions, but Concur Travel sits in Premium, which is quoted. Per-report pricing rises with filing volume, so a sales team filing weekly costs more to support than an equal-size team filing monthly. Per-user pricing reverses that math, so which model costs less depends on your filing pattern.


Configuration is the second complaint. When approval chains live with an admin or implementation partner, raising a meal limit becomes a ticket with a wait.


Travel budgets add pressure. According to[Deloitte's 2025 Corporate Travel Survey](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/about/press-room/deloitte-announces-corporate-travel-study-2025) , more than half of U.S. travel managers surveyed named cost a top-three factor restricting travel in 2025. That's up from 48% in 2024.


Business cases often cite[a 2015 GBTA Foundation study](https://gbta.org/how-much-do-expense-reports-really-cost-a-company/) , conducted with HRS, that put the cost of processing an expense report for a single-night hotel stay at $58 and 20 minutes. It also found 19% of reports had errors costing an additional $52 and 18 minutes to fix.


I'd push back on building a switching case on those figures. They describe one narrow report type, measured more than a decade ago. Measure your own cost per report before you multiply anything.


### When staying on Concur is the right call


Sometimes staying is the better decision. Concur's breadth is hard to replace if you run SAP ERP, manage multi-country VAT and compliance, or need travel, expense, and invoice in one system.


Splitting those configurations across vendors can cost more in integration and control testing than the renewal increase you're trying to avoid.

## Which Concur alternatives cover both travel and expense?


Navan, Perk, and Emburse each book travel and capture expenses, so they replace Concur Travel and Concur Expense together.


According to the[U.S. Travel Association's Spring 2026 forecast](https://www.ustravel.org/sites/default/files/2026-05/US_Travel-Forecast_Spring26.pdf) , U.S. business travel spending was $316.7 billion in 2025, about 86% of its 2019 level in inflation-adjusted dollars. How travelers pay matters as much as where they book, which is why booking policy and[corporate travel cards](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/corporate-travel-card-guide) usually get decided together.


### Navan


Navan combines booking and expense in one app. It issues its own corporate cards and, through Navan Connect, also supports eligible Visa, Mastercard, and American Express corporate cards. Navan Business is for companies up to 300 employees, and Enterprise is quoted.


Choose Navan if booking is the main reason you're leaving. Confirm multi-entity handling in the demo, and ask which ERP connectors come with the plan you'd buy.


### Is Navan a good alternative to Concur?


It is for travel-heavy teams within the Business plan's size limit or on Enterprise. The trade-off is a bet that booking adoption will drive expense compliance. When travelers book elsewhere, you're back to matching, so ask how card transactions from your existing issuer reach Navan.


### Perk


Perk publishes its travel tiers, with a per-booking fee plus a monthly platform fee on paid tiers. Its pricing page lists Perk Card cashback as "coming soon" and supports any card feed, so teams bring their current cards. Choose Perk if you want booking costs you can model from a public page, and note the SAP connector sits on the Pro tier.


### Emburse


Emburse sells Emburse Expense Enterprise (formerly Chrome River) and Emburse Expense Professional (formerly Certify), plus travel booking, AP, and Emburse Cards as an add-on. It comes closest to Concur's breadth. Pricing isn't published, so expect a quote-driven process much like your renewal.


### Is there a Concur alternative that costs less to run and still handles travel?


Vendors that publish travel and expense pricing can be compared on paper, including Navan Business, Perk's travel tiers, and Zoho Expense's self-booking add-on. Quoted suites need a quote built on your own trip and report volume. Run every option against last year's actual trips.


## Which Concur competitors include their own corporate card program?


Ramp, Brex, and Corpay pair their own corporate card program with expense capture. Concur brings corporate card data in through bank card feeds from the card program you already have.


The difference shows up at month-end. When card and expense come from one provider, the transaction, receipt, and GL code start in one system. With a feed, you wait on an issuer file, so ask how long a swipe takes to appear.


According to the[Federal Reserve's 2025 Payments Study](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/other20260701a.htm) , U.S. noncash payments reached 236.6 billion in 2024. Cards accounted for over three quarters by number, and credit card payments grew faster than debit for the first time in almost a decade. Those figures cover all consumer and business payments, so treat them as broad context.


### Ramp


Ramp combines its corporate card with expense, bill pay, and travel booking through Ramp Travel, which launched June 3, 2024. It publishes a free tier, a per-user Plus tier with a platform fee, and custom Enterprise pricing. NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Acumatica, and Business Central sync sits on Plus, which suits teams wanting one platform that includes booking.


### Brex


Brex offers corporate cards, expense, bill pay, and travel, and it has been part of Capital One since April 7, 2026. It publishes a free Essentials tier covering up to two entities, a per-user Premium tier, and custom Enterprise pricing. Choose Brex if you want card, travel, and bill pay together.


### Commercial cards with managed expense


Corpay runs a commercial card program that includes the Corpay Mastercard, the Corpay World Elite Mastercard for business travel, and single-use virtual cards. It pairs that program with Corpay Expense Management for receipt capture, automated coding, approvals, and ERP sync.


Choose Corpay if you're leaving mainly over expense-side cost and complexity and want rebates on card spend. Corpay's card and expense products don't include a flight-booking tool, so a company that needs booking pairs Corpay with a travel tool.


Outside this group, Navan and Emburse offer cards alongside booking, and Expensify offers an optional card. If your current program carries terms you want to keep, a card-agnostic tool may fit better. Our guide to[choosing a commercial card](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/best-commercial-card) covers what to compare.


## Which expense-only tools replace Concur expense?


Expensify, Zoho Expense, Sage Expense Management (formerly Fyle), and Rydoo replace Concur Expense without forcing a card or booking decision. They work with the cards you already carry.


This group keeps the change small, since your card program and possibly your booking tool stay put. Our overview of[expense report software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-report-software) covers the core capabilities to test.


### Expensify


Expensify pairs SmartScan receipt capture with third-party card feeds and an optional Expensify Card. It publishes per-member pricing. NetSuite and Sage Intacct sync require the Control plan, so a mid-market team on either ERP should price Control from the start.


### Zoho Expense


Zoho Expense is free for up to three users and has low per-user paid tiers, with self-booking travel as an add-on. ERP and HRMS integrations are a paid add-on, so check that line first if you run a mid-market ERP.


### Sage expense management


Sage Expense Management is card-agnostic, with real-time feeds on existing Visa, Mastercard, and American Express cards. Sage announced the Fyle acquisition July 28, 2025. Sage Intacct integration sits on the Business tier.


### Rydoo


Rydoo combines expense with AP and books travel through partners, including BCD Travel, Amex GBT Egencia, and Perk. Pricing is per user with a five-user minimum.


Across this group, the plan tier often decides ERP fit more than the product does. Several of these tools put mid-market ERP connectors one tier up, so price the tier you'll actually need. Field-heavy teams should test[mobile expense management](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/mobile-expense-management) on real phones during the trial, since receipt capture decides adoption.

### Which SAP Concur alternatives fit a mid-market company?


No single vendor fits every mid-market team. On NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Business Central, or Acumatica, shortlist one vendor per replacement type that lists your ERP connector at the tier you'd buy. Then score each finalist on the same seven checks.


1.


ERP integration depth, including entities, cost centers, and journal posting


2.


Card feeds versus an own-card program


3.


Policy and approval rules finance can change without a ticket


4.


Travel booking needs, including whether Concur Travel stays


5.


Per-user versus per-report pricing against your report volume and active users


6.


Contract terms, including the notice period


7.


Fraud controls, such as[card-level limits](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/card-controls-spend-policies) and duplicate detection


Each check comes back to control and risk, and the last one deserves extra weight. According to[AFP's 2026 Payments Fraud and Control Survey](https://www.financialprofessionals.org/about/learn-more/press-releases/Details/over-75-percent-of-us-firms-experienced-payments-fraud-in-2025-while-ai-adoption-for-fraud-mitigation-lags) , 76% of U.S. organizations surveyed experienced attempted or actual payments fraud in 2025. That figure spans all payment types, and our guide to[expense fraud detection](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-fraud-detection-prevention) covers how it shows up in T&E.


Two requests separate a real evaluation from a staged one. Ask for a reference customer of roughly your size on your ERP. Then watch an admin change an approval rule live in a production tenant, since demo environments are configured to make that look easy.

## What does migrating off Concur involve?


Migrating off Concur is mostly a data and timing exercise. You need an exit date, a cutover plan for open reports, rebuilt policies and approvals, a card change, and ERP mapping.


Work through these steps in order:


1.


Confirm the contract end date and notice period.


2.


Count open trips and unsubmitted reports at cutover.


3.


Export historical reports and receipts for audit retention.


4.


Rebuild your expense policy in the new tool.


5.


Recreate approval chains and delegates.


6.


Switch the card feed or move to a new card program.


7.


Map GL accounts, entities, and cost centers to the ERP.


8.


Train users and run one parallel close.


The card change is the step teams underestimate. Transactions from the old feed keep arriving after cutover, so someone has to own reconciliation across both systems for at least one cycle.


Name that owner before go-live and give them a clear matching process, ideally backed by[card reconciliation software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/credit-card-reconciliation-software) .


Reimbursements need the same care, since employees with claims in flight should know which system pays them. Test the[expense reimbursement software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/expense-reimbursement-software) in your new tool on a real payroll cycle before the old one shuts off.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best alternative to SAP Concur?


It depends on why you're leaving. Navan, Perk, and Emburse suit teams moving booking and expense together. Ramp, Brex, and Corpay suit card-and-expense consolidation, and expense-only tools suit teams keeping their cards. If the card-led route matches your reason,[see how Corpay's commercial card programs work](https://www.corpay.com/commercial-cards) .


### Who are Concur's main competitors?


Navan, Perk, and Emburse compete as travel-and-expense suites, and Ramp, Brex, and Corpay as card-led platforms. Expensify, Zoho Expense, Sage Expense Management, and Rydoo are expense-only tools, and Coupa is a procurement-led spend suite. We compete on the card-led side, where Corpay Expense Management works with[the Corpay Mastercard](https://www.corpay.com/commercial-cards/corpay-mastercard) .


### Is Ramp cheaper than Concur?


It depends on your filing pattern. Ramp prices per user with a free tier, while Concur prices Base and Plus per report and quotes Premium. Model both against last year's report volume and active users. Rebates also change the net cost of a card-led program, so[talk to our team](https://www.corpay.com/contact-us) to model Corpay against your spend.


### Which is better, Expensify or Concur?


Expensify fits teams that want fast setup and card-agnostic capture, while Concur fits companies with complex multi-country compliance or SAP ERP. Check which Expensify plan carries your ERP sync, since NetSuite and Sage Intacct sync require Control. If vendor payments are on your list too, ask how[single-use virtual cards](https://www.corpay.com/commercial-cards/virtual-cards) could run alongside your expense tool.


### Can you keep Concur travel and replace Concur expense?


Yes, in principle. Confirm how itineraries booked in Concur Travel reach the new expense tool and how card transactions get matched to them. Our card and expense products don't book flights, so that split suits Corpay. If travel spend is moving to a dedicated card,[the Corpay World Elite Mastercard](https://www.corpay.com/commercial-cards/world-elite-mastercard) is our business travel card.
